message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported record results for the fiscal third quarter ended July 31, 2026, with revenue of $1.85 billion and net income of $397 million [D1]. Revenue rose 36.54% and net income rose 107.85% from a year earlier, and the net margin was 21.51% [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of $1.35 billion and operating income of $458 million, up 86.18% from a year earlier [D1]. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of $501 million and operating income of $155 million, up 68.48% [D1]. Total segment operating income was $613 million, up 81.36% from $338 million a year earlier [D1].

Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and earnings per share to $3.34 to $3.40 on approximately 172 million diluted shares [D1]. The mid-point of that revenue range represents growth of approximately 37% from a year earlier [D1]. Management said it was raising its outlook for the fourth quarter and for the full fiscal year on the momentum it had seen [D3]. Management said wireline delivered record orders that more than doubled from a year earlier, driven by rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem [D3]. Management said its order funnel stood at an all-time high and that it expected fourth-quarter orders slightly above the third quarter's level [D4]. Management said the integration of its recent acquisitions was largely complete, one quarter ahead of schedule, and that the supply chain would remain the governor of near-term revenue [D3].

The results beat the analyst consensus for both earnings and revenue, and the fourth-quarter guidance came in above the consensus forecasts [D2]. Management said demand was far exceeding its ability to supply and that the pipeline continued to grow [D3]. Analysts pressed on whether that demand was sustainable and whether supply constraints were capping the guidance, and management described supply as a governor of its ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. Management also said the one-time tariff impacts in the current fiscal year would not repeat, leaving a higher comparison for future profitability [D3]. The quarter's performance was attributed to increased test intensity as design margins shrink, requiring testing at the signal, bit and protocol levels [D4].

Short-term sell-side price targets imply further upside from the recent trading level, and consensus earnings estimates for the current year moved higher with no negative revisions over the past month [D5]. The same commentary warns that price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide [D5]. Related analysis argues that AI growth is strong but that the valuation leaves little room for error, while another argues that further stock price gains are unsupported by fundamentals [D3].
